score_rationale: Strong willingness-to-pay validated by active commercial market: multiple vendors (PostcardMania, HOA Contact Lists, Exact Data) currently selling HOA and community association mailing lists with pricing ranging from $0.10-$0.50 per record for bulk lists (10,000+ HOAs = $1,000-$5,000 typical purchase). Five high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) home services contractors (landscaping, pool maintenance, roofing, painting, paving, pest control) bidding on HOA master contracts worth $10,000-$500,000/year per association, (2) property management software vendors (AppFolio, Buildium, TownSq, HOA Express) selling $100-$500/month SaaS to 350,000+ HOAs nationwide, (3) professional services firms (HOA attorneys, reserve study consultants, engineering firms, insurance brokers) targeting association board clients with $5,000-$50,000/year service contracts, (4) amenity and infrastructure vendors (playground equipment, fitness centers, security systems, EV charging stations) selling capital improvement projects to HOAs with $50,000-$500,000 budgets, and (5) direct mail and marketing agencies serving the HOA vertical. Public data sources include county property records (many counties list HOA affiliation in deed restrictions or CC&Rs), state corporation registries (HOAs register as nonprofit corporations or unincorporated associations), Secretary of State business entity searches, and HOA directories published by Community Association Institutes (CAI) chapters. Zero PII — all association-level business data (HOA name, mailing address, board contact where public, unit count, amenities). Engineering lift is moderate-to-high: scrape county assessor databases for deed restrictions mentioning HOA names, cross-reference against state corporation registries, parse community names from subdivision plat maps, and deduplicate. No low-cost flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad — existing vendors sell multi-thousand-dollar annual subscriptions or per-record pricing. Audience size is massive: approximately 350,000-400,000 HOAs nationwide managing 75+ million housing units (per CAI 2026 data), creating a TAM of 20,000+ B2B buyers (contractors, software vendors, service providers). Score is 7 due to validated high willingness-to-pay from multiple commercial vendors, confirmed public data availability across counties and state registries, proven B2B buyer demand, and absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives — tempered slightly by moderate-to-high engineering complexity due to fragmented multi-source data collection.

data_wanted: HOA and community association data is publicly available via multiple fragmented sources requiring aggregation: (1) County property records and assessor databases — many counties include HOA affiliation in deed restrictions, CC&Rs (Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions), or subdivision plat maps; scrape property records for subdivision names and HOA references (e.g., 'subject to covenants of [HOA Name] recorded at Book X Page Y'); (2) State corporation registries and Secretary of State business entity searches — HOAs register as nonprofit corporations or unincorporated associations in most states; search for entities with keywords 'Homeowners Association', 'HOA', 'Community Association', 'Property Owners Association', 'POA', 'Condominium Association'; (3) Community Association Institute (CAI) chapter directories — some CAI state chapters publish member HOA directories or association management company client lists; (4) Municipal planning and zoning records — some cities publish subdivision master plans listing HOA governance structures. Key fields per association: HOA/community association legal name (e.g., 'Sunset Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc.'), mailing address (often a PO Box or management company address), city, state, ZIP, county, approximate unit count (number of homes/condos/townhomes managed — derive from subdivision plat maps or management company descriptions), property type (single-family, condo, townhome, mixed-use, age-restricted 55+), and board contact information where publicly listed (president, treasurer, or management company contact — availability varies; many HOAs list only PO Box). Target all active associations only — exclude dissolved or merged HOAs. Scope to residential community associations — exclude commercial property associations, industrial park associations, and timeshare/resort HOAs. Approximate count: 350,000-400,000 HOAs nationwide managing 75+ million housing units (per CAI 2026 statistics: 29% of US housing stock in HOA/condo/co-op governance). Target output: 350,000-400,000 rows. Data is public per state corporation disclosure laws (nonprofit entity filings are public) and county property records sunshine laws, though fragmented collection requires multi-source scraping and deduplication.

Even a 1% bid win rate (3,500 proposals sent, 35 contracts won at $20K average = $700K revenue) yields 8,800× ROI against $79 data cost. (2) Property management software vendors: HOA tech platforms generate $100-$500/month per association ($1,200-$6,000/year); a $79 TAM database of 350K HOAs provides complete market for email campaigns, webinar funnels, and direct mail — acquiring 100 new customers (0.03% conversion) at $3,000/year LTV = $300K revenue against $79 cost. (3) Professional services firms: HOA attorneys, reserve study consultants, and insurance brokers targeting associations with $5,000-$50,000/year recurring contracts can justify $79 for a complete prospect universe — one new client at $10K/year = 125× ROI. (4) Amenity vendors: capital improvement projects (playgrounds, fitness centers, EV chargers) range $50,000-$500,000; vendors prospecting 1,000 HOAs from a $79 database need only one project win to break even. (5) Direct mail agencies: marketing firms serving the HOA vertical charge $0.50-$2.00 per direct mail piece; a $79 database enabling them to offer clients 'targeted HOA campaigns' creates service differentiation and upsell opportunity. The active market confirmed by PostcardMania, HOA Contact Lists, and Exact Data (with typical list pricing at $0.10-$0.50 per record = $35,000-$175,000 for full 350K database) proves B2B buyers pay thousands for HOA data.
